t:
(a) 
There are authorized to be appropriated, for the purpose of financial assistance and administrative expenses under sections 104 and 106, not to exceed $12,000,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1967, and not to exceed $12,000,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1968.
 
    (b) 
There are authorized to be appropriated, for the purpose of financial assistance and administrative expenses under sections 105, 106, and 107, not to exceed $400,000,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1968, and not to exceed $500,000,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1969.
 
    (c) 
Appropriations authorized under this section shall remain available until expended.

fable.w: This section only authorizes appropriations for financial assistance and administrative expenses and sets their availability. A tempting reading is that "financial assistance" implies dealings with outside parties, but funding grants is not consultation, and applications for grants are excluded by the definition. No outside party is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue over any federal decision.
fable.s: There are authorized to be appropriated, for the purpose of financial assistance and administrative expenses under sections 104 and 106

qwen_block.w: This section solely authorizes the appropriation of funds for financial assistance and administrative expenses. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or participation with entities outside the federal government. The definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or grants, and this text is merely a funding authorization.
qwen_block.s: There are authorized to be appropriated, for the purpose of financial assistance and administrative expenses under sections 104 and 106, not to exceed $12,000,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1967, and not to exceed $12,000,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1968.

opus.w: This section only authorizes appropriations and says the funds stay available until spent. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue, so no one outside the federal government takes part in a federal decision. The phrase "financial assistance" points at most to grant funding, and the definition excludes applying for grants or benefits.
opus.s: There are authorized to be appropriated, for the purpose of financial assistance and administrative expenses under sections 104 and 106, not to exceed $12,000,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1967
